arxiv-2110-02299.title: Twisted two-dimensional material stacks for polarization optics
arxiv-2110-02299.creator: Kaveh Khaliji, Luis Martín-Moreno, Phaedon Avouris, Sang-Hyun Oh, Tony Low
arxiv-2110-02299.description: Abstract The ability to control light polarization state is critically important for diverse applications in information processing, telecommunications, and spectroscopy. Here, we propose that a stack of anisotropic van der Waals materials can facilitate the building of optical elements with Jones matrices of unitary, Hermitian, non-normal, singular, degenerate, and defective classes.

arxiv-2201-04128.title: Cavity engineering of Hubbard U U via phonon polaritons
arxiv-2201-04128.creator: Brieuc Le Dé, Christian J. Eckhardt, Dante M. Kennes, Michael A. Sentef
arxiv-2201-04128.description: Abstract Pump-probe experiments have suggested the possibility to control electronic correlations by driving infrared-active phonons with resonant midinfrared laser pulses. In this work we study two possible microscopic nonlinear electron-phonon interactions behind these observations, namely coupling of the squared lattice displacement either to the electronic density or to the double occupancy.

arxiv-2204-11570.title: Corrections to electroweak precision observables from mixings of an exotic vector boson in light of the CDF W W -mass anomaly
arxiv-2204-11570.creator: Chengfeng Cai, Dayun Qiu, Yi-Lei Tang, Zhao-Huan Yu, Hong-Hao Zhang
arxiv-2204-11570.description: Abstract We enumerate various effective couplings that contribute to the mixings between an exotic vector boson Z ′ Z^{\prime} and the neutral electroweak vector bosons. The miscellaneous mixing patterns can be evaluated perturbatively. The effective oblique parameters S ′ S^{\prime} , T ′ T^{\prime} , and U ′ U^{\prime} are calculated to compare with the electroweak precision test results.

arxiv-2205-13076.title: On Bridging the Gap between Mean Field and Finite Width in Deep Random Neural Networks with Batch Normalization
arxiv-2205-13076.creator: Amir Joudaki, Hadi Daneshmand, Francis Bach
arxiv-2205-13076.description: Abstract Mean field theory is widely used in the theoretical studies of neural networks. In this paper, we analyze the role of depth in the concentration of mean-field predictions, specifically for deep multilayer perceptron (MLP) with batch normalization (BN) at initialization.

arxiv-2310-07207.title: Robust Safe Reinforcement Learning under Adversarial Disturbances
arxiv-2310-07207.creator: Zeyang Li, Chuxiong Hu, Shengbo Eben Li, Jia Cheng, Yunan Wang
arxiv-2310-07207.description: Abstract Safety is a primary concern when applying reinforcement learning to real-world control tasks, especially in the presence of external disturbances. However, existing safe reinforcement learning algorithms rarely account for external disturbances, limiting their applicability and robustness in practice. To address this challenge, this paper proposes a robust safe reinforcement learning framework that tackles worst-case disturbances.

arxiv-2401-10589.title: Rethinking the Soft Conflict Pseudo Boolean Constraint on MaxSAT Local Search Solvers
arxiv-2401-10589.creator: Jiongzhi Zheng, Zhuo Chen, Chu-Min Li, Kun He
arxiv-2401-10589.description: Abstract MaxSAT is an optimization version of the famous NP-complete Satisfiability problem (SAT). Algorithms for MaxSAT mainly include complete solvers and local search incomplete solvers. In many complete solvers, once a better solution is found, a Soft conflict Pseudo Boolean (SPB) constraint will be generated to enforce the algorithm to find better solutions.

arxiv-2409-16200.description: Abstract Over the past decade, Magnetic Resonance Fingerprinting (MRF) has emerged as an efficient paradigm for the rapid and simultaneous quantification of multiple MRI parameters, including fat fraction (FF), water T1 ( T ​ 1 H ​ 2 ​ O T1_{H2O} ), water T2 ( T ​ 2 H ​ 2 ​ O T2_{H2O} ), and fat T1 ( T

arxiv-2507-19699.title: Towards Inclusive NLP: Assessing Compressed Multilingual Transformers across Diverse Language Benchmarks
arxiv-2507-19699.creator: Maitha Alshehhi, Ahmed Sharshar, Mohsen Guizani
arxiv-2507-19699.description: Abstract Although LLMs have attained significant success in high-resource languages, their capacity in low-resource linguistic environments like Kannada and Arabic is not yet fully understood. This work benchmarking the performance of multilingual and monolingual Large Language Models (LLMs) across Arabic, English, and Indic languages, with particular emphasis on the effects of model compression strategies such as pruning and quantization.

arxiv-2508-20393.title: The frequency-independent radio luminosity – orbital/rotational period relation of RS CVn stars
arxiv-2508-20393.creator: Qichen Huang(黄启宸), Biwei Jiang(姜碧沩)
arxiv-2508-20393.description: Abstract Radio emissions from RS CVn objects exhibit distinct characteristics at low and high frequencies, widely attributed to differing radiation mechanisms. The disparate processes of high-frequency gyrosynchrotron and low-frequency electron cyclotron maser emissions have traditionally suggested an absence of correlation in their radio luminosities.

arxiv-2601-15324.title: Prometheus Mind: Retrofitting Memory to Frozen Language Models
arxiv-2601-15324.creator: Mark Wind
arxiv-2601-15324.description: A 2026 arXiv research paper by Mark Wind. Adding memory to pretrained language models typically requires architectural changes or weight modification. We present Prometheus Mind , which retrofits memory to a frozen Qwen3-4B using 11 modular adapters (530MB, 7% overhead)—fully reversible by removing the adapters. Building this system required solving four problems: (1) Extraction —we develop Contrastive Direction Discovery (CDD), which finds semantic directions via minimal pairs without labeled data. (2) Training —end-to-end optimization collapses; stage-wise training of each adapter on simple proxy tasks succeeds.

pmc-11507340.title: Sharing for Caring? A Patients’ and Clinicians’ View on Handling Personal Medical Data in the Context of Digitization: An Exploratory Study
pmc-11507340.creator: Kevin Frank, Thorsten Mengesdorf, Marija Radić, Philipp Herrmann, Arno Appenzeller, Henrik Mucha, Berna Orak, Indra Spiecker gen Döhmann, Stefan Rüping, Harald Burkhardt, Michaela Köhm, Stephanie Dauth, Daniele Giansanti
pmc-11507340.description: Background: The healthcare sector is currently undergoing a significant transformation, driven by an increased utilization of data. In this evolving landscape, surveys are of pivotal importance to the comprehension of patient needs and preferences. Moreover, the digital affinity of patients and physicians within the healthcare system is reforming the manner in which healthcare services are accessed and delivered.

pmc-11604177.title: Duct of Luschka Bile Leak With Formation of Biloma Post-Cholecystectomy: A Case Study
pmc-11604177.creator: Jamie McDermott, Nima Sadeghi, Dayna Telken, Imtiaz Ahmed
pmc-11604177.description: A rare complication of laparoscopic cholecystectomy is a biloma, which usually develops as a result of the dissection of non-visible, abnormal ducts of Luschka. This anatomical variation in the bile ducts was initially overlooked within the biliary tree. While it generally holds minimal clinical significance, it may occasionally lead to bile leakage following cholecystectomy.

pmc-11672824.title: Decay of Airborne Bacteria from Cattle Farm Under A-Band Ultraviolet Radiation
pmc-11672824.creator: Luyu Ding, Qing Zhang, Ligen Yu, Ruixiang Jiang, Chunxia Yao, Chaoyuan Wang, Qifeng Li
pmc-11672824.description: Simple SummaryA-band ultraviolet (UVA) in solar radiation plays an important role in the natural decay of airborne bacteria. In this study, laboratory simulation experiments were conducted to investigate the impact of varied UVA intensities on the decay of airborne bacteria and to analyze the potential use of UVA to reduce indoor airborne bacteria in cattle houses.

pmc-12729994.title: Sustainable Management of Filamentous Algae in Freshwater Ecosystems: Insights from Cladophora sp. Life History, Reproductive Tactics, and Growth Ecology
pmc-12729994.creator: Liangjie Zhao, Liangxin Guo, Chenxi Tan, Yongtao Tang, Yuanye Ma, Zhen Zhang, Yongxu Cheng, Chen Qian
pmc-12729994.description: Simple SummaryCladophora blooms have become a widespread problem in freshwater ecosystems, degrading water quality and endangering aquatic life. To control its biomass, we systematically examined the life history and reproductive tactics of a freshwater Cladophora sp., quantifying propagule release and growth under varying nutrient and ecological conditions.

pmc-13124275.title: Health system strengthening recommendations for lung cancer care: lessons from the COVID-19 pandemic
pmc-13124275.creator: Elysse Bautista-González, Mercedes Aguerrebere, Anne Peasey, Hynek Pikhart, Cecilia Vindrola-Padros
pmc-13124275.description: We explore how the COVID-19 pandemic amplified barriers across the lung cancer care continuum in Mexico. Drawing from a cross-sectional qualitative arm of a mixed-methods study (N = 46), interviews were conducted with lung cancer patients at the Mexican National Cancer Institute between 2020 and 2021.

pmc-13133598.title: RIPK3 Inhibition Mitigates Denervated Muscle Atrophy via NOX4‐Mediated Mitochondrial Restoration and Inflammation Suppression
pmc-13133598.creator: Yuntian Shen, Chen Zhang, Zihao Zhao, Jia Yi, Xinlei Yao, Bingqian Chen, Hualin Sun
pmc-13133598.description: BackgroundPeripheral nerve injury‐induced muscle atrophy shares core pathophysiological features with systemic wasting disorders including cachexia and sarcopenia, yet early molecular triggers remain undefined. This study investigates the pathogenic role of receptor‐interacting protein kinase 3 (RIPK3) in denervation atrophy.MethodsSciatic denervation was induced in rats for initial time‐course transcriptomics and in mice for genetic and pharmacological studies.

pmc-13211274.title: MscaVPR: Multi-Scale Coordinate Attention Network for Robust Visual Place Recognition
pmc-13211274.creator: Xiaohan Gao, Zhinong Zhong, Yongjian Tan, Ning Jing, Anran Yang, Qingren Jia
pmc-13211274.description: Visual place recognition (VPR) aims to localize a query image by matching its visual representation against a geotagged database. One major challenge in VPR is to learn place representations that remain robust under appearance changes, viewpoint variations, and perceptual aliasing.

pmc-13219836.title: A chromosome-level reference genome for Pacific herring (Clupea pallasii) from the Bering Sea
pmc-13219836.creator: Laura E. Timm, Yin-Chen Hsieh, J. Andrés López, Sydney A. Almgren, Jessica R. Glass, Laura Timm, Laura Timm
pmc-13219836.description: Pacific herring (Clupea pallasii) serve as a critical trophic link between plankton and many marine species targeted by fisheries. With a broad distribution throughout the North Pacific Ocean, from the Arctic to temperate latitudes, herring hold ecological, economic, and cultural importance. Despite this importance, genomic resources for this species, such as reference genome sequences, have only recently become available.

pmc-13450002.title: Liver donor macrosteatosis is associated with adverse long-term outcomes exclusively in metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease recipients: a U.S. transplant registry analysis over the last decade
pmc-13450002.creator: Leandro Sierra, Butros Fakhoury, Kanisha Bahierathan, Maria Saavedra-Martinez, Maria Ortega Abad, Lily Liu, Vinay Jahagirdar, Pojsakorn Danpanichkul, Katherine M. Cooper, Luis Antonio Diaz, Juan Pablo Arab
pmc-13450002.description: BackgroundLiver grafts with >30% macrovesicular steatosis (Mas30) have shown acceptable long-term graft survival (GS) in steatotic liver disease (SLD) recipients. However, grouping SLD etiologies under a single umbrella ignores their distinct metabolic profiles and may lead to suboptimal allocation decisions.
